Application
Application Instructions:
The interdisciplinary Neuroscience and Neurotechnology Ph.D. program at Georgia Institute of Technology welcomes applications from students with undergraduate training in a broad range of areas, including psychology, biology, mathematics, engineering, and computing.
Prospective students apply through Georgia Tech’s online graduate application (see below). First, you should carefully review faculty research interests as the application asks you to identify your top three faculty that you prefer as your research/thesis advisor. Our program does not operate exclusively as a direct-admit program; however, applicants are asked to identify faculty members whose research interests align with their own, and faculty interest is an important consideration during the admissions process.
For applicants who are not directly admitted to a faculty member’s laboratory, rotation opportunities are available. However, because rotation funding is limited, applicants whose proposed faculty advisor is willing and able to provide funding may have a stronger likelihood of admission. Note: we do not require students to rotate. Similarly, if none of the selected faculty members are interested in mentoring or funding a student, the likelihood of admission may be reduced.
Thus, prospective applicants are encouraged to contact potential faculty mentors before applying to discuss research interests and laboratory opportunities. While such communication does not guarantee admission, it can help applicants identify faculty whose research interests, availability, and funding align with their goals. Furthermore, while providing a preliminary selection of an advisor and school/department helps the admissions process, it does not restrict your selection of a different advisor or school/department at a later stage.
To be eligible to serve as student research supervisors in our PhD program in Neuroscience and Neurotechnology (NSNT), a faculty member must have a formalized affiliation with the Georgia Institute of Technology. Through Georgia Tech’s partnership with Emory University, faculty in the Coulter School of Biomedical Engineering are eligible to supervise NSNT students.
During the application process, you will be prompted to select one of the following two admissions pathways:
PhD in Neuroscience and Neurotechnology in the School of Biological Sciences
PhD in Neuroscience and Neurotechnology in the School of Psychology
PhD in Neuroscience and Neurotechnology in the School of Biomedical Engineering
You should select the admissions pathway associated with the school/department of the research/thesis advisor you select as your first choice (the advisor’s home school/department is identified in the link provided above). If the school/department of your selected research advisor does not appear above, then please apply through the Biological Sciences pathway. Note: while providing a preliminary selection of advisor and school/department helps the admission process, it does not restrict your selection of a different advisor or school/department at a later stage. You may also select faculty within your list from different schools. Students who are unsure of which homeschool/department to apply to should direct their questions/emails to our Program Director, Dr. Tim Cope, for guidance.
For example: you could select Dr. X (Biological Sciences) as your first choice, Dr. Y (Biomedical Engineering) as your second choice, and Dr. Z (Psychology) as your third choice. You would then apply for a PhD in Neuroscience and Neurotechnology in the School of Biological Sciences. You might, however, ultimately end up with Dr. Z (Psychology) as your research/thesis advisor, or, after rotating, select Dr. B (Mathematics).
A list of schools/departments in which students at Georgia Tech pursue research interests in neuroscience and neurotechnology:
Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering
School of Psychology
School of Biological Sciences
School of Physics
School of Mathematics
School of Chemistry and Biochemistry
School of Electrical and Computer Engineering
School of Computational Science and Engineering
Regarding test scores (GRE and English Proficiency Test Minimum Scores):
GRE scores are not required
TOEFL: 100 (IBT, minimum score of 19 for each section)
IELTS: 7.5 (minim score of 6.5 each for listening, reading, speaking, and 5.5 for writing)
